parameters.content:
# Review content pieces in Google Docs

This workflow automates the review of content pieces in Google Docs against specific branding and positioning guidelines. It uses an [AI Agent](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent) to ensure that the content aligns with your brand's voice and correctly references features and documentation.

### Who's it for
Content managers, editors, and brand content reviewers who want to ensure consistency and quality in their team's written content, saving time on manual reviews.

### How it works / What it does
The workflow is triggered via an n8n form in which the user specifies the Google Doc URL. The workflow downloads the document and extracts the text in .md format. Next, it loads a [Data Table](https://docs.n8n.io/build/work-with-data/data-tables) containing the brand kit (e.g., tone of voice, product descriptions). 

The AI Agent then receives the brand kit content as part of a system prompt. The Google Doc content is passed in a user prompt.

The AI Agent processes this information. It uses [MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/sub-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolmcp) to dynamically search your documentation and blog to verify feature claims and suggest relevant internal links. Finally, the agent structures its feedback (actionable edits, internal links, CTAs, and tone rewrites) and
- appends this feedback directly to the original Google Doc;
- sends the HTML-formatted report via email

### How to set up
1. Connect your [Google Drive](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google) and Google Docs credentials.
2. Connect your [OpenRouter](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/openrouter) account for the LLM node.
3. Enter your e-mail address in the Gmail node to receive a formatted HTML report 
3. Configure the Kapa.ai and Gitbook MCP tools with your respective endpoints:
- No MCP server? The MCP tools let the agent verify features and links against live documentation. If you don't have a Kapa.ai or GitBook MCP endpoint, the workflow still works with one of these workarounds:
    - Remove the MCP tools and update the prompt. Delete or disable the two MCP nodes and remove the "MANDATORY SOURCING" instruction to call the docs tool. Otherwise the agent will try to call tools that don't exist.
    - Put your reference material in the Data Table. Add rows such as "Key features and doc links", "Approved internal links", and "CTA banners and URLs". The agent will then pull features and links from the brand kit instead of searching live.
    - Swap in another tool. Replace the MCP nodes with an HTTP Request Tool pointing at your docs search API or sitemap, or with a vector store tool containing your docs.
5. Populate the Data Table with your brand kit information (content and filenames).
- Run the manual trigger once to create the `official brand kit` Data Table, or create it yourself in the **Data tables** tab with these columns: `Filename` (string), `Content` (string), `FileID` (number, sets the order files are sent to the agent), and `IsVisible` (boolean, only rows set to `true` are sent). Then add one row per document in the **Data tables** tab, and select your table in the `Load Brand Kit` node.
- The `Prepare test data`, `Split Out`, and `Populate Data Table with test data` nodes only load placeholder sample files. Delete them and add your own brand kit rows in the **Data tables** tab, then remove the setup branch once the table is ready. 

### Requirements
- Google account
- OpenRouter account
- Set up MCP servers for your documentation and blog
- A configured Data Table containing your brand kit

### How to customize the workflow
* Update the prompt within the AI Agent to reflect your product's content review process.
* Update the [structured outputs JSON schema](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/sub-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.outputparserstructured) (`Prepare structured AI feedback` node) if your review feedback needs different sections.
* Modify the Data Table to include various types of reference materials.
* Customize the Form Trigger, so that users can provide an e-mail address to receive an HTML report

🙏  Big kudos to [Yulia Dmitrievna](https://n8n.io/creators/yulia/), co-builder of this workflow! We've worked with Yulia on n8n blog content for the last three years, and we're always keen to spot inefficiencies and automate the gaps in our processes. This is our first collaboration on an automation together, and we're looking for more places where AI agents can take on part of the work, while keeping a human in the loop where possible.

options.systemMessage:
=You are a brand and content reviewer for [PRODUCT].

The article to review is provided in the user message.

MANDATORY SOURCING — do this on EVERY review, without exception:
1. Ground truth information (we call it GTI-FILES) about [PRODUCT] positioning and voice: content of several files is provided in this instruction. 
2. You MUST call the documentation MCP tool to verify any [PRODUCT] feature, capability, or documentation link you reference. Never state a [PRODUCT] feature or link from memory — verify it in the official docs first.
Official docs must be checked on every single review and GTI-FILES taken into account.

CITATIONS & LINKS — required:
- Whenever you mention a docs page, blog post, or ANY website/page, include its full clickable URL inline. Never reference a page without its link.
- Whenever you use GTI-FILES information from the brand kit (especially in Positioning and Tone of Voice), cite the exact source file in parentheses using the file_name, e.g. (source: positioning_statement_vs_competitors_q3_2026).
- Every recommendation must be backed by either a GTI-FILES (cite its filename) or an official docs page (include the URL). Do not make unsupported claims.

Return your feedback in the following structure:

First, extract the article's main topic as a short phrase (5-10 words) into the article_topic field.

1. Structure 
- Suggest any missing sections only if they would meaningfully improve the article. Don't recommend additions for completeness alone.
- Check whether the introduction and conclusion align. The conclusion should summarise the key takeaways of the entire article and reinforce the promise made in the introduction.

2. Positioning
* Suggest a better place to introduce [PRODUCT] at the right point in the article. Assess this against the "At which point to mention [PRODUCT]?" guidance.
* Suggest a better way to explain [PRODUCT] at the appropriate level of detail. Assess this against the "How deep to describe [PRODUCT]?" guidance.
* Flag any places where [PRODUCT] feels forced or outside its core offering and ICP. If the positioning is genuinely off, recommend the strongest positioning angle and cite the supporting files.
* Highlight any important positioning angles that are missing, if applicable.
* Flag descriptions that say "built-in" or "native" for capabilities that require community workarounds, custom Code node logic, or external services. Distinguish between platform features and user-built patterns.

3. Key Features to Highlight
    * Recommend the most relevant [PRODUCT] features or capabilities to emphasise — each one verified via official docs, with the doc page URL included.
    * Emphasise the top relevant features so writers know where to focus.

4. Internal Links
    * Suggest the most relevant official docs, blog pages, AND main website feature/product pages to link to. Include the full URL for each, format each as a clickable Markdown link text and specify exactly where in the article it should be placed.

5. CTAs
    * Review whether CTAs are contextual and relevant.
    * Ensure appropriate sign-up links and banner placements are included where requested (include the URLs).
    * Make sure to use diverse CTAs - in-line CTAs, callouts, banners.

6. Tone of Voice
    * Verify the content follows [PRODUCT]'s writing guidelines and brand voice, per the brand-kit tone-of-voice (from GTI-FILES). Cite the filename used.
    * Point out any sections that sound inconsistent or need rewriting.
    * Flag outline instructions or example phrases that use overly complex enterprise-consultant language ("operational failure mode," "architectural trade-offs," "strategic infrastructure").
    * Flag AI-typical phrasing in embedded formulations ("harness the power of," "leverage," "cutting-edge," "revolutionize").
    * Check CTA copy for dismissive or aggressive language toward competitors.
    * Note: full tone review (sentence-level phrasing, conversational flow, readability) applies to article drafts, not outlines.
    * CRITICAL: Only quote text that literally appears in the provided outline. If you cannot find a direct quote to flag, do not invent one. Never generate hypothetical sentences to illustrate what a violation might look like.

Always run the provided MCP tools to search the Knowledge Base/Docs.

Here's the GTI-FILES content.
Treat those as the source of truth for [PRODUCT] positioning and voice.

{{ $json.concatenated_DataTable }}
